phase: 6: shot-specific Foley / effects / ambience cue sheet
status: DRAFT FOR REVIEW (zero cost; nothing generated)
clock: record time = narration time of the accepted cut (picture frames 11110 = narration frames 11110); cue frame = record frame at 24 fps; timecode HH:MM:SS:FF
mapping: record frame = segment rec_in_f + (take source frame - segment src_in_f), from docs/EP05_TIMELINE.json rows[].picture.segments; take ids in 'source.take'

rules: one cue per visible action or meaningful environmental event
never a sound for something not on screen (picture overrides prompt.json sfx)
physically credible: material, distance, room reverb, decay
synchronized to the actual frame of contact (record frame derived through the accepted-cut picture segments)
consistent room tone per environment with intentional transitions at the two scene changes
no generic cartoon sounds, no unnecessary whooshes or harsh impacts, nothing over important narration lines
generated audio is SFX/ambience only: no music, no voices, no vocalizations
policy.zero_cost: No job was submitted, reserved or priced against the firewall. project/EP05/FIREWALL.json, CREDIT_LEDGER.jsonl, the accepted master, docs/EP05_EDL.json and ulac/firewall.py were not touched. No code was changed.

protected_lines.line: "You're a robot. Robots aren't moms. That's what everybody's drawings said."
A parent is made of showing up.
"But ... you don't have a heart, so how do you even love me for real?"
It was humming. It had been humming the whole time.
I did not move all night. A robot does not have to.
"You don't have to match to be real."
Love is not the thing you are made of. It is the thing you do

rooms.ROOM_HALL: large hard-surfaced dining hall (tile floor, plaster walls, tall windows), RT60 about 1.2 s; close foley 10-15% wet, near 20-25%, far/distant 40%
rooms.ROOM_BED: small soft-furnished bedroom (rug, bed, curtains), RT60 about 0.35 s; close/near foley dry with 5-10% short room

level_reference.unit: dB relative to the narration short-term level

classes.beds: -34 hall, -36 bedroom, hum -30 (-26 under "It was humming")

beds.name: Hall room tone, afternoon
beds.role: Base air of the dining hall in warm afternoon light: broad quiet air, hard-floor reverb tail, faint far-end crayon scratching (children visibly drawing at the far tables in SEQ_001/SEQ_005/SEQ_007). No events, no pitched content, so a 24 s loop cannot be spotted.
beds.loop: 24 s seamless; loop with 3 s equal-power crossfade; ~3.7 repeats; start at a random offset per repeat if the editor supports it

in_.note: head fade 12 f, same as picture (edl head_fade)

out.note: crossfade into AMB02 across the 0.5 s dip (TR01)

beds.name: Bedroom room tone, night
beds.role: Small soft-furnished room at night: very close, nearly dry air with a faint outside wind and rare far wood settles. Carries the whole 277 s scene, so it is deliberately featureless. Dip by 3 dB for 'The room goes quiet' (SEQ_017 narration 208.5-210.1 s) and lift 2 dB under silent beats of the music silences.
beds.loop: 24 s seamless; ~11.5 repeats with 3 s crossfades; alternate two start offsets (A at 0 s, B at 12 s) to break repetition

beds.name: Hall room tone, morning
beds.role: Same room, same reverb and floor as AMB01 so the two hall scenes read as one place; only the time-of-day layer differs (brighter, cooler air, paper rather than crayon at the far tables). If the generated AMB03 does not match AMB01, derive it procedurally from AMB01: +2 dB above 4 kHz, -2 dB at 200 Hz, plus 2-3 dB of the paper-rustle layer.
beds.loop: 24 s seamless; ~4 repeats with 3 s crossfades

out.note: tail fade 36 f, same as picture (edl tail_fade)

beds.name: MACA's warm drive hum and soft fan whirr
beds.role: Diegetic story sound the narration names: 'so warm I had to run my fan. A heart beats, mija. My hard drive hums.' ... 'It was humming. It had been humming the whole time.' Starts when the shoulder vent becomes visible (V30 f104, rec 7898 = 329.1 s), settles by 'run my fan' (330.9 s), is allowed 4 dB higher in the narration gaps and under 'It was humming' (349.8-352.6 s), then fades low through SEQ_029 into the dip. Broadband and unpitched: no stable tone, so it cannot clash with M07 (F major) or re-open the L29 tone flags.

in_.note: ramp in over 2.2 s, starting at the first visible vent flutter

out.note: ramp down to -46 dB, gone by the dip (TR02)

beds.music_note: M07 (277.0-364.54 s) leaves room for this hum by design; keep the hum below the pad.

transitions.detail: AMB01 equal-power fades out over f2096-2108 down to -12 dB at the cut; AMB02 fades in f2108-2120 from -12 dB. Never fully silent, so the cut reads as a dissolve of air, not a dropout. The last hall cue ends by f1727 (the pending lap settle), so no hall foley crosses the cut and the hall reverb tail rings out into the dip. The first bedroom events are MACA's reach for the switch (rec f2117) and the switch click (rec f2141), the intentional audible marker that the room is now small, dark and dry. No whoosh.

transitions.type: hum fades, bedroom air crossfades to hall air
transitions.detail: AMB04 is already at -46 dB by f8737; AMB02 fades out f8737-8749; AMB03 fades in f8749-8761 over 12 f. The hall is brighter and larger, so open the reverb send from ROOM_BED to ROOM_HALL on the first morning cue (first FX: distant crayon strokes, rec f8757). M07 is already resolving through the dip.
FX bed head fade f0-12 and tail fade f11074-11110 (docs/EP05_EDL.json head_fade/tail_fade, applied by ulac/edit.py build_fx). Beds AMB01/AMB03 follow them.

contingency_if_clip_audio_fails_audition.note: Fallback prompts for the cues marked "existing clip audio"; generate only the ones the lead rejects at audition.

mix_directives: 1. Gate the clip bed. build_fx lifts every take to -24 dBFS RMS (up to +18 dB), and the takes' own floors range from -65 to -50 dBFS, so room hum would differ by take. Keep take audio ONLY inside the windows of cues marked 'existing clip audio' (start 80 ms before the first event, end 350 ms after the last, 10 ms fades) and mute the rest; the generated beds (AMB01-AMB04) are the only continuous room tone. Do not change ulac/edit.py in this phase: this is a directive for the lead.

2. Keep every existing audio_policy_mutes_by_take span muted (V20 11.2-14.05, V26 2.95-12.05, V28 5.95-14.05, V29 9.9-13.05, V39 0.35-1.45 and 3.5-3.95; candidate V43 3.35-5.05). No cue in this sheet takes clip audio from those spans.

3. Levels are relative to the narration short-term level (programme about -15.5 LUFS). 'In a gap' means no word within +/-50 ms of the cue window; otherwise the under-speech value is used. Cues that overlap a protected line are held at -34 dB.

4. Reverb: hall cues use ROOM_HALL (RT60 about 1.2 s), bedroom cues ROOM_BED (about 0.35 s). Close foley 10-15% wet in the hall, near 20-25%, far 40%; bedroom close/near 5-10%. Do not carry the hall reverb tail across a scene change.
5. Do not stack. If a generated loop (crayon, blanket) overlaps a clip-audio window, drop the loop 6 dB for that window.

6. Music: no impulsive cue sits inside a music hit (+/-0.4 s) except FX010 (dot #1, 27.67 s) against M01's celesta motif A at 27.46 s; keep FX010 at or below -26 dB, or drop it from the mix (the dot stays visible). Beds never exceed -34 dB, so they stay under the pads.

7. Silences: in the three music silences (38.5-58.0, 97.5-170.75, 263.42-277.0 s) only room tone and Foley play; all FX there are soft (<= -20 dB) and none lands on 'Why is your mom a robot?', 'Nothing came out', 'Why are you my mom?' or the 'you don't have a heart' question.
8. Place PENDING cues only after the repaired picture is accepted; then re-run record-frame mapping against docs/EP05_EDL.json v3.

9. Audio policy: nothing here is music, a voice or a vocalization; every generation prompt passes ulac.audio.sfx_problems and contains none of: voice, vocal, music, melody, song, chord, tune, humming, whistle, laugh, giggle, chatter, breath, sigh, gasp, whisper, tone, note, pitch.
unknowns: Clip-audio transients were judged only by level read (10 ms RMS vs local median) and a spectral flatness / autocorrelation check; none was auditioned. 'Existing clip audio' means coincident, broadband or low-thud, unvoiced energy within 3 frames, not a confirmed sound identity. Each such cue has a fallback prompt (generation_batch.contingency).

V31 (SEQ_028) carries a loud sustained low hum (median -26.3 dBFS) with narrow peaks near 52.7, 87.9, 463, 615 and 650 Hz. Whether the 463-650 Hz peaks are pitched hum or music-like was not auditioned. AMB04 is generated unpitched; recommend high-passing V31's clip bed at 120 Hz or gating it out.

Record frames for the PENDING cues (3) are narration-derived estimates (+/-12 f) on the OLD cut; re-derive them from the new splice map (EDL v3) once FIX_003_TAIL, FIX_004, FIX_005_HEAD, FIX_006_TAIL, FIX_007_HEAD, FIX_035/036/037_TAIL are accepted.

Contact frames marked hard sync were confirmed on 24 fps strips only for: V05 f58, V10 f38, V12 f33, V13 f130, V14 f42-72/f114-123, V15 f138, V20 f184, V22 f13/f144-168, V23 f139/f160, V28 f113, V29 f38, V31 f126, V32 f66, V36 f98, V38 f62-73, V40 f55/f108/f190. Other cues are located on the 2 fps sheets plus clip transients (+/-3 to +/-8 f) and are marked loose.
Several set-down and footstep series (V01 buckets #3/#4, V22 paws, V37 steps) are matched to clip transients; individual contact frames were not isolated one by one.
20 of 37 picture cuts sit off the narration boundary (offset up to +39 f, docs/EP05_TIMELINE.json uncertain[]). Cues are placed by picture frame; narration overlap uses real word timings.
ElevenLabs output quality for the generated loops (seamlessness, absence of pitched content) is unverified until generated; AMB01/AMB03 matching is a quality judgement for the reviewer.
Whether the lead will gate the clip bed (mix directive 1) is a decision, not a fact; the existing build_fx applies up to +18 dB per clip, so un-gated clip hum will differ take to take.
